results: 1. Focused neurologic examination of cranial nerves, including facial movements, forehead wrinkling, eye closure, cheek puffing, and smiling
cranial nerve examination: bilateral post-paralytic facial synkinesis; narrowed left palpebral fissure
2. Complete motor, sensory, coordination, gait, and reflex examination
deep tendon reflexes and plantar responses: normal
gait, ability to run, and limb sensation: normal
ear and mastoid examination: normal, no vesicles
5. MRI of the brain with and without gadolinium contrast, including the brainstem and internal auditory canals
MRI brain and internal auditory canal with contrast: no tumour, no perineural enhancement, no central lesion
6. Electroneurography and needle electromyography of the facial muscles
needle electromyography: chronic bilateral facial neuropathic changes with synkinesis
electroneuronography / facial EMG: chronic reinnervation with synkinetic co-activation; no active denervation
7. Hemoglobin A1c and fasting lipid panel
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Chronic bilateral post-paralytic facial synkinesis due to recurrent idiopathic facial nerve palsy (bilateral Bell palsy), without active denervation

Alternative 1: Sequelae of prior bilateral Lyme neuroborreliosis

Alternative 2: Congenital bilateral facial nerve dysfunction (Möbius-spectrum disorder)

Alternative 3: Chronic bilateral facial neuropathy associated with an inflammatory or autoimmune disorder
